blocks.p: Angel puts stock back on the shelves of the station. The *Character* window holds what he carries; the *World* window holds the containers around him.

The title bar of each window counts the containers open in it, and each container has a column of its own. Each column header gives the container's name, its weight against what it holds at most, and the number of items in it. To move an item, drag it from one column to another.

caption: Figure 8-1
The Character window: the backpack and the inventory.

blocks.p: Angel's backpack holds the stock: candy, chips, cigarettes and colas. The row of the item being dragged is lit in its column.
The two buttons at the right of a column header choose how the column shows its items: as a list of names or as a grid of pictures. The backpack is shown as a list and the inventory as a grid.
A row with a count, such as *Diet Cola x2*, is a stack; its weight is given in parentheses.

marks.text: The title bar counts the containers: 2 here,
Each column header shows its weight and item count.
Drag an item from one column to another to move it.

sticky.text: Stocking the shelves, one drag at a time.

blocks.p: The *World* window opens a column for each container in reach. The buttons down its left side list them; in the Fossoil they are three shelves and the ground. The ground is a column of its own, like any shelf.
Figure 8-2 shows the *World* window while a Diet Cola is dragged from the backpack to the first shelf. While you drag, the item shows at the pointer with its weight.
A column that holds nothing says so. Under each header, *Name* and *Wt* head the column's list.
Every column works the same way, whether its container is a shelf or the ground. A container has a column only while it is in reach.

caption: Figure 8-2
The World window: three shelves and the ground.

blocks.p: Drop the item on a column to put it in that container. The shelves of the station hold the stock: the first holds jerky, candy and chips; the second batteries, candles, rope and a hose.

marks.text: Here, a Diet Cola is dragged to the first shelf.
These buttons list the containers in reach: three shelves and the ground.
The ground is a column too. Nothing is on it here.
Each shelf in reach has its own column.

sticky.text: Three shelves and the ground, all in reach.
